title: The d- and f-Block Elements: Chapter Introduction
subject: Chemistry
objective: Iron bridges, copper wires and bright blue, purple and orange solutions all come from one part of the periodic table. The d-block (groups 3–12) fills d orbitals; the f-block (two rows below) fills f orbitals. Variable oxidation states, colour, magnetism and catalysis make them special.

fill.q: The d-block occupies groups 3 to ____ of the periodic table.

tf.q: The f-block is placed in two separate rows at the bottom of the periodic table.
Transition metals usually show only one oxidation state.
tf.explain: They show variable oxidation states (Mn: +2 to +7).

ar.r: Colour is one of the special properties of the d-block.

ar.a: The f-block is drawn below the main table.
ar.r: Each f series has 14 elements that would widen periods 6 and 7.

mcq.q: Which is NOT typical of transition metals?

num.q: How many electrons can an f subshell hold?

short.q: Name four special properties of transition metals.
short.solution: Variable oxidation states, coloured compounds, paramagnetism, catalytic activity (also complexes, alloys, high melting points).
